text:
alex: Quick smoke this morning — ran a short A100 vs H100 sweep for Mosaic-7B (stock fp16 + q4_0) and Llama2-7B (q8_0) across us-east1 / eu-west1 / asia-south1. High level first: H100 consistently lower p50/p99 prefill and higher decode tps; A100 sometimes shows slightly lower $/1M when kernels stay on the fast path. Raw notes below.

sam: awesome — did you keep seq/batch the same across runs?

alex: yes: seq=2048, batch=8 (logical requests), kv-enabled. same workload traces (short chatty prompts + 512 token responses). driver/runtime: our nightly runtime build (rtd-2026-03-05).

priya: can you paste the run command? makes repro easier.

alex:
```
./run_bench --model mosaic-7b --quant q4_0 --gpu a100 --region us-east1 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv_cache --warmup 50 --runs 200
```
(alike for h100, and for llama2-7b with q8_0)

alex: Summary numbers (median of 3 runs per region, avg over runs):
- Mosaic-7B q4_0 (us-east1):
  - A100: prefill p50 21ms, p99 58ms; decode 4.2k tok/s; ~$10.8 / 1M tokens
  - H100: prefill p50 13ms, p99 34ms; decode 6.6k tok/s; ~$8.6 / 1M tokens
- Mosaic-7B q4_0 (eu-west1): H100 decode drops ~8% vs us-east (5.9k tok/s) due to a kernel fallthrough observed on some CUDA versions. A100 similar pattern but larger p99 tail (~70ms).
- Mosaic-7B q4_0 (asia-south1): both see token/sec drop; H100 5.2k, A100 3.6k. region net egress and noisy hosts likely contributing.

- Llama2-7B q8_0 (us-east1):
  - A100: prefill p50 28ms, p99 85ms; decode 3.4k tok/s; ~$12.1 / 1M tokens
  - H100: prefill p50 17ms, p99 45ms; decode 5.3k tok/s; ~$9.0 / 1M tokens

jonah: those $/1M numbers assume our current reserved pricing? what's the exact cost model you used?

alex: good call — used per-hour GPU list price (on-demand-ish) + host overhead 15%, then normalized to tokens/sec. Not committed pricing. If you plug committed A100 SKU discounts the A100 $/1M can drop ~20% and can invert the $ gap for some workloads.

priya: you mentioned kernel fallthrough in eu-west for H100 — can you expand?

alex: yes. On h100 we observed occasional dispatch to a fallback attention kernel for certain sequence-length mod patterns. This shows as ~10-15% throughput regressions and higher p99 prefill. Happens on runtime rtd-2026-03-05 + CUDA 12.3 stack; not reproducible on our internal CUDA 12.4 promo build.

sam: any quality regressions from q4_0 vs q8_0?

alex: quick eval on 500 prompts: negligible diff for casual chat; for targeted factual QA q4_0 had small drop (BLEU/EM style slice) ~1.8 points on our narrow eval. We're flagging a candidate for a longer eval.

benchbot: benchmark-summary: models=[mosaic-7b,llama2-7b], gpus=[a100,h100], regions=[us-east1,eu-west1,asia-south1], seq=2048, batch=8, runs=3

alex: ops notes / next steps:
- Run a parity test with CUDA 12.4 variant across eu-west1 to confirm kernel fix.
- Sweep batch sizes 4/8/16 for latency-sensitive routes — H100 gains more at larger batch due to better vector throughput.
- Recompute $/1M with committed pricing tiers and our infra amortization model; baseline above is on-demand style.
- Longer quality eval for mosaic q4_0 (1k prompts, stratified by QA vs chat).

priya: can you add a quick chart (tokens/sec vs region) to the perf dashboard? makes it easier to digest.

alex: will upload a lightweight CSV to the eng-ml-s3 and link after I rerun eu-west w/ CUDA12.4.

sam: nice work. if eu-west fix holds, H100 looks like the clear perf lead for prefill/throughput; cost choice depends on committed discounts and kernel stability. :thumbsup:

alex: yup. cc @jonah on scheduling the infra CUDA bump for a small canary fleet.
